header: Date: 2026-10-13 | Time: 14:00-14:52 UTC | Duration: 52 minutes | Attendees: Laura Chen (Redwood AE), Miguel Soto (Redwood SE), Ravi Patel (Skybridge PM), Sofia Morales (Skybridge Tech Lead), Evan Brooks (Skybridge Marketplace Ops)
summary: Technical sync to align on marketplace listing requirements, reference architecture for a joint marketplace offering, and next steps for a lightweight joint solution. Covered onboarding checklist, security/compliance expectations, integration points (SaaS redirect vs private listing), and a plan to run a benchmark on Skybridge infra. Some transcription noise on product names (e.g., "Redwood Optima" appears instead of Redwood Optimize) and a few mis-heard acronyms.
topics: Reference architecture (VPC/private listing vs hosted integration)
Auth and security: SSO/SAML, RBAC, KMS and audit logs
Deployment options: Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private (VPC/on-prem)
Benchmark plan and metrics (latency, throughput, cost)
transcript: [00:00] Laura Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining — Laura from Redwood here. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Ravi Patel: Hi, Ravi here from Skybridge, PM on the marketplace effort.
[00:09] Sofia Morales: Sofia — tech lead, joining from our infra team.
[00:12] Evan Brooks: Evan, I run marketplace operations at Skybridge.
[00:16] Miguel Soto: Miguel (SE) from Redwood, I’ll walk through the reference arch and the terraform bits.
[00:22] Laura Chen: Great — agenda: listing checklist, reference arch options, security questions, benchmark plan, and next steps.
[00:30] Ravi Patel: That sounds good, we mostly want to understand what you need to list and how to make the integration low-friction.
[00:36] Sofia Morales: Also, our infra people want to confirm network requirements — VPC peering vs private listing, egress, that sort of thing.

[00:42] Miguel Soto: Yeah, we'll sketch both. For a marketplace "private listing" we usually recommend a VPC peering with a controlled egress path and optional VPC endpoint for the control plane. For hosted we can do SaaS redirect — fewer infra changes but different compliance posture.
[00:58] Evan Brooks: When you say "control plane" can you clarify? Do you need us to open ports or is it outbound only?

[01:05] Miguel Soto: Mostly outbound — the control plane makes api calls to your listing service, so an outbound TLS egress is sufficient. For dedicated/backplane variants we sometimes request a private connection, but that's optional.
[01:16] Sofia Morales: Okay outbound only is easier. But our security team will want SOC 2 docs and details on KMS and audit logs.
[01:23] Laura Chen: Absolutely. We'll include our SOC 2 report, encryption at rest description (KMS/HSM), and audit log retention options in the security packet — I'll attach those to the checklist.
[01:33] Ravi Patel: Are there any folks who need a signed DPA or specific data residency guarantees for the marketplace listing?

[01:39] Laura Chen: We have a standard DPA and can add residency clauses for EU data, or we can offer a private deployment if you need on-prem or dedicated isolation. That would be a different commercial track.
[01:49] [Speaker 1]: (murmur) question about latency numbers — do you have sample metrics?

[01:52] Miguel Soto: Yes, I can share our typical 95th p50 numbers for hosted models, but those vary by model and seq length. Also note we sometimes refer to our "Redwood Optima" — that's a mis-transcription; it's Redwood Optimize internal tooling, sorry for the confusion.
[02:08] Sofia Morales: For the marketplace cert, our reviewers will want to run a quick benchmark. What's the minimum footprint we should plan for?

[02:16] Miguel Soto: For small workloads you can run a 1-gpu instance with our optimized kernels, but for predictable throughput we recommend our dedicated pool (2+ GPUs) depending on concurrency. We'll provide a small terraform snippet to spin up the test harness.
[02:29] Evan Brooks: About marketplace listing metadata — what fields do you require? Can we pre-populate the product page?

[02:36] Laura Chen: We'll provide a checklist: product name, short/long descriptions, logos, privacy statement, SLA, pricing tiers, and an integration guide. We'll also include sample webhooks and health-check endpoints.
[02:47] Ravi Patel: Pricing — do you publish usage-based pricing or do you require a committed plan for marketplace?

[02:52] Laura Chen: Both are possible. For initial listing we usually publish a hosted pay-as-you-go price. For enterprise customers through the marketplace we can surface reserved/dedicated plans as contractual add-ons.
[03:02] Sofia Morales: Security again — audit logs and SSO. We need SAML/SSO integration for our marketplace admin flows. What's supported?
[03:09] Miguel Soto: We support SAML SSO and OIDC, plus scoped RBAC. For marketplace admin we recommend creating a service account with least privilege for the listing operations.
[03:18] [00:03:20] Sofia Morales: Sorry, slight lag on my side — could you repeat the RBAC recommendation?
[03:23] Miguel Soto: Sure — create an "integration" role with limited permissions: listing:read, listing:publish (temporary), logs:read. Use short-lived tokens or KMS-wrapped keys for automation.
[03:36] Ravi Patel: On the reference architecture, can you walk through the VPC peering flow and the fallback options?

[03:41] Miguel Soto: Walkthrough: if you choose private listing we recommend VPC peering for the control plane and use a private endpoint for the model runtime. If peering isn't allowed, we fallback to secure outbound only with mTLS and strict IP allowlist. We'll include diagrams in the doc.
[03:58] Evan Brooks: Any special network ports? Our firewall team wants specifics.

[04:01] Miguel Soto: Standard HTTPS/TLS port 443 for API traffic, plus health-check endpoints on 8443 if you want internal checks — but we can keep everything on 443. We'll put exact CIDR ranges in the terraform snippet.
[04:12] Sofia Morales: Great. About billing — do we need to handle metering or will Redwood push invoices?

[04:18] Laura Chen: For marketplace listings we typically integrate with the marketplace billing flow. Redwood still reports usage and can reconcile. For dedicated/reserved contracts we invoice directly.
[04:27] Ravi Patel: Competitors question — our marketplace team asked how you differ from CloudMart and VendorX in terms of integration friction.

[04:34] Laura Chen: Main differentiators: runtime optimizations for lower cost/latency, unified tooling across hosted/dedicated/private, and detailed ops docs for marketplace publishing. We'll include a short comparison deck.
[04:44] Miguel Soto: Also, our runtime selects kernels depending on seq length and hardware which helps CPU/GPU unit economics compared to generic endpoints.
[04:54] Sofia Morales: We wanted to confirm if you support quantized model variants for lower-cost tiers in the marketplace.

[05:00] Miguel Soto: Yes, we support quantized variants and can expose them as alternate SKUs in the marketplace. We'll document recommended fallback policies so customers hit a cheaper variant if the premium model is constrained.
[05:11] Evan Brooks: For publishing windows — we have a weekly publish process on Tuesdays; what's your SLA for review?
[05:17] Laura Chen: We'll aim to review artifacts within 3 business days; for code/terraform we typically take 5 days for a technical review. We'll align with your Tuesday windows.
[05:26] Ravi Patel: Ok — if we get the docs in by next Monday we could aim for the next Tuesday publish.
[05:30] Laura Chen: Perfect. We'll also include a small sample app you can run to generate metrics for the benchmark.
[05:36] Miguel Soto: I'll share a helm chart and a small k8s job that runs a set of synthetic calls to measure p95 latency and throughput.
[05:43] Sofia Morales: For the benchmark, what metric thresholds do you expect to see to certify a listing?

[05:49] Miguel Soto: Typical gate: p95 < 700ms for common generative tasks at 1 token/sec average; throughput depends on concurrency. But it's flexible — we'll consider your expected workload. We'll capture exact thresholds in the checklist.
[06:02] Ravi Patel: Any legal artifacts we should prepare?
[06:06] Laura Chen: Standard DPA, IP terms, and an optional addendum for dedicated/private deployments. Evan — your marketplace ops will probably want sample support SLAs.
[06:14] Evan Brooks: Yes, send the SLA template please.
[06:17] Laura Chen: Will do — I'll attach SLA examples + support path.
[06:22] Sofia Morales: A quick question on telemetry — can you pass structured logs to our observability?
[06:27] Miguel Soto: Yes, we have export hooks (Kafka, S3, or HTTP) and can push structured event logs. We'll include sample config.
[06:34] Ravi Patel: There's some discussion around offering Redwood Dedicated as a marketplace SKU. How would that look?

[06:39] Laura Chen: Dedicated would be a contractual SKU surfaced on the marketplace as an "enterprise offering" — the booking flow would redirect to sales for provisioning. We'll outline the ops playbook.
[06:48] Sofia Morales: We might need a quick security deep-dive later with your security team if we go dedicated.
[06:53] Laura Chen: Absolutely — we can schedule a security review (SOC2 walk-through and architecture whiteboard) after initial artifacts are shared.

[06:59] Miguel Soto: One more thing — for fallback policies, we usually recommend a three-tier fallback: premium model -> quantized variant -> cached responses for repeated prompts. That reduces cost and preserves availability.
[07:13] Evan Brooks: Do you have an example listing page we can look at?

[07:16] Laura Chen: Yes — I'll send a link to an example listing and the reference arch doc. (link placeholders: https://redwood.ai/docs/marketplace-checklist, https://redwood.ai/reference-arch/skybridge)
[07:24] Ravi Patel: Perfect. Anything else on the infra side?
[07:28] Sofia Morales: Just to confirm, will the terraform snippet include CIDR and module references?
[07:32] Miguel Soto: Yes, it will include a module for peering, security groups, and the service account with minimal IAM.
[07:39] Laura Chen: Ok let's recap next steps — me for docs and listing checklist, Miguel for ref-arch and terraform, Sofia for sample metrics, Evan for marketplace windows.
[07:51] Ravi Patel: Sounds good. We'll aim to have the metrics and initial artifacts to you by next Monday.
[07:56] Laura Chen: Great — will follow up with a calendar invite for the benchmark run. Thanks everyone.
[08:01] Sofia Morales: Thank you — talk soon.
[08:03] Miguel Soto: Thanks, bye.
[08:05] Evan Brooks: Bye.
[08:07] [End of recording]
